slides.reasoning: Design B delivers the brief's condensed futurist numerals, a dramatic glowing lime curve with labeled points and a tightly gridded metric column, while Design A's generic bold sans, off-brand red/cyan chart dots and empty lower-right area weaken both palette compliance and hierarchy.

Design B is a genuinely illustrated hand-drawn route with clay dominance, marigold accents and a taped note, whereas Design A is a flat centered timeline on blush with large dead zones and a stray tilted buddy box.

Design B builds a precise enterprise before/after with a tangled vermilion graph versus an ordered azure identity graph, clean rules and aligned metric rows, while Design A's clip-art arrow, overlapping connector lines and floating dots read unresolved.

Design B's orbital allocation ring with gold segments, centered $240M and restrained serif hierarchy matches the institutional brief exactly, while Design A defaults to a standard donut plus a legend that duplicates the percentages.

Design B is a true keynote reveal—brushed-silver ground, oversized ARC ONE wordmark, exploded driver stack with signal-red callouts—while Design A relies on a dim generic headphone photo with a hard split edge and small spec list.

Design B is a coherent monospaced navy scorecard with one revenue-vs-plan curve, variance markers and an emphasized activation gap bar, whereas Design A's descending line misleadingly plots unrelated regions and its 'ACTIVATION / TARGET 75%' labels collide.

Design B delivers the requested custom transit-map diagram with interchange and north-star measures in wayfinding type, while Design A reduces the pillars to four unequal bar rules and an awkward oversized black 'North Star' circle.

Design B's stepped chevron swimlanes with citron gate diamonds, week ruler, owners and team dot-count read as a dynamic roadmap, while Design A's four flat blocks with dashed gate lines and unlabeled gate descriptions are closer to the boxy layout the brief warned against.

Design B renders a bold circular 4C loop with arrowed flow plus a marker-annotated worked example, while Design A's overlapping bubble cluster has cramped text inside circles, disconnected diagonal ticks and a large empty lower half.

Design B pairs an expressive 100-square 68% waffle with an actual fragmented three-app journey diagram and editorial serif headline, whereas Design A's plain donut and three labeled circles are generic and leave the cobalt quote bar floating.

Design B captures the auditorium keynote moment with oversized dissolving display type, a real visible/hidden UI diagram and a silhouetted crowd, while Design A stacks a banner headline over dim stock audience photography with awkward boxes and centered all-caps text.

Design B's orange/powder-blue split with oversized editorial numerals, aligned metric rows and a properly attributed quote is confident and structurally tight, while Design A leaves large orange voids, inconsistent number alignment and a quote box with an oddly stranded label.

Design B makes an illustrated corridor map the informational centerpiece with scale bar, legend and a field-ledger card in the specified sage/ochre/river-blue palette, while Design A's stock aerial photo with disconnected orange dashes reads as arbitrary graphic overlay rather than a mapped corridor.

Design B's enormous annotated 'a' with numbered leader lines, yellow counter fill and a same-baseline three-face comparison is genuinely instructional, while Design A's small letterform, floating rule-to-label lines and black spec panel are far less legible as teaching.

Design B's collage citrus macro, aqua sector bar and dotted leader list form an energetic editorial composition, whereas Design A's photo panel has a visible tonal seam, a transparent overlay box clipping the image edge and near-invisible contact text.
